sections.title: New Dates and a New Theme
sections.content:
M.I.T.'s Project MAC agreed to host the next Network Working Group (NWG) meeting in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Because of scheduling conflicts, the dates in RFC 207 moved ahead two weeks. The meeting starts on Sunday, October 10 at 12 noon and adjourns on Thursday, October 14.

Until then the NWG had been almost entirely concerned with communications and protocol implementation. Implementation was now substantially complete and usage of the network had emerged as a primary concern, so the theme is network usage. The meeting is to demonstrate current host capabilities, identify areas of application, address issues for users and service centers, and give updated status information.
sections.plainLanguage: The group finished building the roads and now wants to talk about where people can drive.

sections.title: The Three Phases
sections.content:
The first phase is the system programmers workshop, from Sunday October 10 at 12 noon through Monday October 11. The second phase begins Tuesday October 12 at 9:30 a.m. and offers a protocol review, a course in NIC usage, and a session for TIP users.

The third phase begins Wednesday October 14 with status reports: in the morning the workshop outcome, the protocol review results, specifications for on-line co-operative interaction, NIC philosophy and user-level protocol development, and in the afternoon the ILLIAC IV, TENEX and Data Computer developments and a discussion of network management. Thursday morning has a round table on access to service centers via the network.
sections.plainLanguage: First the builders compare notes, then there are classes and reviews, then everyone reports what is new.

sections.title: Sessions and Logistics
sections.content:
The protocol review is jointly chaired by John Postel (UCLA) and Alex McKenzie (BBN) and is meant to review current standard protocols. The NIC course is a tutorial, with its size limited by the number of available consoles. The TIP session, run by BBN, presents the characteristics of a Terminal Interface MessAge Processor and how to use one to access remote services.

Attendees were asked to register by phone, and a block of rooms was reserved at the Hotel Sonesta in Cambridge on a first come first served basis. More information with a schedule of workshop times and rooms was promised later.
sections.plainLanguage: The note also says who runs each class, how to sign up and where to sleep.
